summary: Run 4 of M1-S04 — a second, narrower § 4 test-only repair, this one after reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 7 (S2-F-12), the same finding that sent M1-S03 back to running a second time. Run 6's fix (§ 0c, S2-F-11) got every test method into System.runAs(agent) with a permissioned user; run 7 then failed all 30 test methods across M1-S03 and M1-S04 at the same @TestSetup seed insert of Case, on fieldNames: AccountId. The cause is in the shared factory, not the test: TestDataFactory.createCases(count, accountId, overrides) assigned AccountId = accountId unconditionally, so Tier2ChannelHealthTest.seed()'s null accountId argument still marked the field populated, and under API 67.0's default user-mode the plain insert inside System.runAs(agent) checked FLS on that populated-but-null field, which the Standard-User-profile agent has no create access to. Fix applied: artefacts/M1-S04/classes/TestDataFactory.cls replaced with a verbatim copy of the corrected templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls (commit 5edcb3281) — diff against the template is empty, confirmed this run. Tier2ChannelHealthSchedulable.cls, Tier2ChannelHealthQueueable.cls and Tier2ChannelHealthTest.cls are all unchanged: the existing seed already called createCases(1, null, overrides) and no test method reads or asserts on Case.AccountId, so no test needed to start passing a lookup explicitly. The three previously-declared checkers were re-run verbatim and still exit 0; the due-diligence check_test_class_standards.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S04/classes run also re-ran, exit 0, ERROR=0, with the same expected WARN (template-class-not-shipped / TestUserFactory, unrelated to this fix). check-outputs is ok on all six declared paths. A parallel repair of the same shape is running on M1-S03; this run touched no file under that step's artefacts.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per GATES.md Gate D: Gate B resolved every symbol this run touches (the factory is a byte-identical copy of a template already grounded, and Tier2ChannelHealthTest's call sites were re-read, not re-derived) and Gate C check 3 (compile) did not run — build_mode is design-only, there is no target_org_alias, and there is no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI. The fix is a mechanical, verbatim template substitution the checker suite (four commands, all exit 0) verifies statically. What would raise this to HIGH is a green dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests or RunLocalTests actually executing the seed insert, which no agent in this loop may perform — that is exactly the gap run 8 of the mock deploy exists to close.

findings.detail: Neither S2-F-11 (run 6) nor S2-F-12 (run 7) was caught by this step's own declared acceptance_tests — three checkers plus xml/manifest — none of which execute Apex or model FLS. check_test_class_standards.py does statically catch the user-mode-test-without-runas rule S2-F-11 fixed, but it is still not in plan.json steps[M1-S04].acceptance_tests (recorded previously as S5-F-02's sibling observation in run 3's envelope); S2-F-12's null-lookup-vs-FLS interaction has no static checker rule at all in this library today and could only be caught by an org-executing dry run.

A rule catching 'lookup arg assigned unconditionally in a factory method' would need to ship in skills/apex/test-data-factory-patterns or test-class-standards — flagging as a library gap, not something to build inline here.

process_observations.observation: The fix required replacing exactly one file with a verbatim, independently-diffed copy of an already-corrected canonical template, and zero changes to any production or test class in this step.

Tier2ChannelHealthTest already called createCases with a null accountId and asserted nothing about Case.AccountId, so the corrected factory's behavior change (leaving the field unset rather than null) required no compensating edit to this step's test seed.

This is the second consecutive repair on M1-S04 driven by a mock-deploy finding rather than by a step-level checker, following the same pattern S5-F-02/S5-F-03 already flagged in run 3 — the library has no static rule for 'a test factory assigns a lookup argument unconditionally', so this class of defect can only be caught by an org-executing dry run.

The 'setup objects in user mode' ambiguity the M1-S04 § 0c repair record left open was never reached by run 7 (the failure occurred earlier, at the non-setup Case/Integration_Failure__c insert) and stays open for run 8.
